title: AviKndr/universal-words
abstract: Answer to Problem 10.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, posed by Yu. I. Merzlyakov in 1986 and still open in the Notebook's 21st edition (2026), in both directions. Positive direction: there are constants C and N0 such that for all nonzero integers r, s with r or s odd, the word x^r y^s is universal on the symmetric group S_n (every permutation is a value) whenever n >= N0 and n >= C * log m(r,s), where m(r,s) is the product of the distinct primes dividing rs. This is the S_n analogue of the logarithmic Brenner-Evans-Silberger bound for A_n; the best previous S_n bound (Droste, 1986) was linear in m. The constant C is effective (the paper gives 4.65 for its fully effective cases), while the threshold N0 is ineffective solely because the proof uses Vinogradov's three-primes theorem. Negative direction, unconditional: the logarithmic shape is optimal. For r = lcm(1..n) with s its odd part, no element of order 3 in S_n is a value of x^r y^s, while log m(r,s) equals theta(n), the full Chebyshev mass of the primes up to n. The proof is machine-checked in Lean 4 on top of Mathlib, with the complete prose write-up included in this repository. The principal theorem, UniversalWords.kourovka_10_32_conditional, is a fully proved implication from eight explicitly stated published theorems (Herzog-Kaplan-Lev, Boccara, three Rosser-Schoenfeld bounds, Montgomery-Vaughan's Brun-Titchmarsh inequality, Vinogradov's three-primes theorem, and the Halberstam-Richert sieve bound) and depends only on Lean's three standard axioms, as does the optimality theorem UniversalWords.not_universal. A quarantined module assumes the eight statements as axioms to recover the unconditional form.
